From: James Hunter <james.hunter@acmefs.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security-review@acmefs.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFI: Vulnerability management questionnaire and SBOM request

Hi Laura,

Thanks for engaging with Acme on the RFP. As part of our security due diligence we need a completed vulnerability management questionnaire (attached template), an SBOM for any runtime components used in the hosted Redwood service, and a recent pen test summary. Specifically we need answers to the following:

- Which SAST/DAST tools do you run (names/versions)?
- What are your patch SLAs for Critical / High / Medium severity vulnerabilities?
- Date and vendor for last external penetration test and a short summary of findings/remediations (redacted OK).
- SBOM format and license declarations for components.
- Any third-party runtime components that require separate licensing/embargoes.

Can you return the completed questionnaire and supporting artifacts by EOD 2026-03-12? We may request a short technical follow-up / call after review. I’ve attached our Acme_vuln_template.xlsx for your use.

Attachment: Acme_vuln_template.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
James Hunter
Security Program Manager
Acme Financial Services
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: James Hunter <james.hunter@acmefs.com>
Cc: security-review@acmefs.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Vulnerability management questionnaire and SBOM request

James —

Thanks for the template. We’ve completed the vulnerability questionnaire and attached the artifacts you requested. Summary below; please let me know if you want a signed attestation on Redwood letterhead — happy to provide.

Executive summary (attachments included):
- SAST: We run Semgrep (v1.22) in CI for language-specific pattern matching and CodeQL (v2.7) for deep analysis on PRs. Rulesets include OWASP Top 10 checks and Redwood custom rego rules for secrets.
- DAST: Public endpoints are scanned nightly with OWASP ZAP. Pre-production and staging run scheduled dynamic scans with Burp Suite Professional; we also run authenticated scans for critical flows.
- Patch SLAs (target windows): Critical = 24 hours (emergency hotfix cadence), High = 7 days, Medium = 30 days. SLA exceptions are documented and require change-approval ticketing; we include compensating controls when a fix is delayed (WAF rules, feature flag isolations).
- Pen test: External pen test completed Q4 2025 by BlueTeam Security. No critical findings. Two high-severity issues were identified and remediated; both mitigations were deployed and verified within 21–30 days. We’ve included a one-page redacted summary (pen_test_summary_redwood_2025Q4.pdf).
- SBOM: Provided as SPDX v2.2 CSV (redwood_sbom_20260309.csv). Components include common OSS (Apache-2.0, MIT), and one third-party proprietary runtime licensed under Redwood’s enterprise runtime agreement (note included in SBOM column "license_notes").

Attachments: redwood_vulnerability_questionnaire_20260309.xlsx, redwood_sbom_20260309.csv, pen_test_summary_redwood_2025Q4.pdf

Next steps: I propose a technical deep-dive to walk Acme’s security team through the SAST/DAST controls and our patch escalation process. How does Fri 2026-03-13 at 10:00 AM PT look for your team?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Accounts Manager
Redwood Inference

Forwarding Acme’s request and the draft response/attachments I sent. Two quick asks before I send the final artifacts to James:

1) Security attestation language: I wrote "No critical findings" in the one-line summary. Vivek, can you confirm we’re comfortable with that phrasing and with sharing the redacted vendor report?
2) SBOM licensing note: Mina, please confirm the wording around the proprietary runtime — they may push for license text or proof of purchase rights. If we need a redaction or specific phrasing, flag it.

I’m planning to attach the redacted pen test one-pager and the SPDX CSV. If either of you needs the original vendor report for review, I can pull it from our secure drive.

Thanks — urgent on this one, Acme asked for completion by 03/12.

—Laura

Laura / team —

Confirmed. I’ve reviewed the pen test one-pager and approve sharing the redacted summary. BlueTeam’s full report is under NDA in our secure drive; redaction removes customer names and IP addresses. Statement is accurate: Q4 2025 external test by BlueTeam, no critical findings, two high severity issues remediated and verified within 21–30 days.

On SLAs: the windows Laura listed are our customer-facing targets. For enterprise customers we can include a contractual SLA for critical issues (24 hours) with a defined escalation path to on-call engineers and dedicated capacity if needed.

I’m copying Priyom and Mina for any legal/licensing comments.

—Vivek

Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A few follow-ups from our review:

1) Can Redwood provide a signed attestation on company letterhead that the Q4 2025 pen test was completed by BlueTeam Security and that there were no critical findings? We need this for our vendor risk register.
2) In the pen test summary you noted two high issues remediated in 21–30 days. Can you provide the specific remediation timeline for each (discovery date -> remediation verification date) in redacted form? We only need dates and a short note about verification steps.

If you prefer, we can put the attestation and the remediation timeline into a DocuSign and route it to your security lead for signature. Also — the technical deep-dive time Fri 03/13 10:00 AM PT works for our team. Please send the calendar invite and dial-in.
